channel.title: Bloomberg — Reuters/Bloomberg pool
channel.description: Provenance-aware feed; classification fields distinguish exact wire copies from citations.

item.title: BlackRock’s Koesterich Sees Energy Stocks as Best Portfolio Diversifier
item.description: Russ Koesterich, Global Allocation Fund portfolio manager at BlackRock, says bonds are not working as a hedge as yields on 30-year US Treasuries rose to the highest since 2007 this week. He talks about the factors he sees driving long-dated bonds and why he doesn’t see $100 oil derailing the US economic expansion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Stock Exchange Lures Two ETFs in First Primary Listings
item.description: The Texas Stock Exchange notched its first primary listings as two small exchange-traded funds focused on the state’s economy announced plans to transfer to the upstart marketplace.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger

item.title: Home Depot Beats Estimates on Faster Sales Growth
item.description: Home Depot’s results beat estimates in the second quarter, as comparable sales, which measure results at stores open for at least a year, rose 1.7%, while adjusted earnings also surpassed expectations. Lindsay Dutch of Bloomberg Intelligence has more on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Iran War: Trump Not Interested in Truce Extension | The Pulse 8/18/2026
item.description:
"The Pulse with Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.
Today's guests: Jimmy Muchechetere, Investec, Senior Equity Analyst & Başak Yavçan, Migration Policy Group, Head of Research (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Emerging Assets Halt Rally on Higher Oil Prices, Bond Selloff
item.description: An emerging-markets equity benchmark snapped a four-day advance and a currency gauge retreated from record highs as a global bond selloff combined with higher oil prices weighed on risk sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Peter Laca

item.title: India Challenges US Quartz Tariffs With WTO Consultation Bid
item.description: India has sought consultations with the US at the World Trade Organization over tariffs imposed by the White House on some quartz products, adding another point of friction between the two countries as they remain without a trade deal.
item.dc:creator: Shruti Srivastava

item.title: Bond Yields Are Hitting Multidecade Highs Around the World
item.description: Everything from inflation to the AI boom is pushing borrowing costs higher.
item.dc:creator: Phil Serafino

item.title: RBI’s Forex Deposit U-Turn Exposes Wider Communication Gap
item.description: A sudden decision by India’s central bank to end a special incentive for attracting foreign-currency deposits a month ahead of schedule has caught bankers, economists and traders off guard and raised questions about how effectively it was communicating with market participants.
item.dc:creator: Anup Roy and Siddhi Nayak

item.title: Alibaba-Backed Robot Maker LimX Said to Plan Up to $300 Million Hong Kong IPO
item.description: LimX Dynamics has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering to raise as much as $300 million, people familiar with the matter said, adding to a wave of Chinese robotics companies lining up to go public.
item.dc:creator: Dave Sebastian, Julia Fioretti and Joanne Wong

item.title: Target Bets on Trendy Snacks and Drinks in Grocery Revamp
item.description: Target has long struggled with its grocery identity: whether it wants to be a discounts-driven everyday chain or a cool zeitgeisty retailer. Its latest big bet indicates it’s chosen the latter. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tata Sons Defers Annual Shareholder Meeting for Lack of Quorum
item.description: Tata Sons Pvt. deferred its annual general meeting after a key shareholder was unable to participate, according to people familiar with the matter, even as the Indian conglomerate prepares to find a new chairman following Natarajan Chandrasekaran’s resignation last week.
item.dc:creator: P R Sanjai

item.title: The Diamond Industry Wants You to Buy "Natural"
item.description: Over the past five years, lab-grown diamonds have shaken his industry to the core. Now, companies like De Beers are battling the avalanche of cheaper, near-identical synthetic gems. Stacey Vanek Smith reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rare $1 Billion IPO Rush Seen in Zambia After Election
item.description: Zambia’s stock exchange expects to bring a record $1 billion of initial public offerings to market after this month’s presidential election, as Africa’s second-biggest copper producer benefits from soaring prices for the metal.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hill and Taonga Mitimingi

item.title: Ardian Taps UBS to Explore Sale of Swissbit
item.description: Ardian is weighing a potential sale of Swissbit, a provider of industrial data storage and security products, people familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Eyk Henning and Swetha Gopinath

item.title: Germany Sells 30-Year Bonds at the Highest Yield Since 2011
item.description: Germany’s borrowing costs hit a 15-year high in a major sale of long-dated bonds, as investors fret about rising government debt and persistent inflation.
item.dc:creator: James Hirai and 'Tofe Ayeni

item.title: Bond Slump Sends Long-Term Debt Costs to Highest in Decades
item.description: Longer-maturity bonds are at the epicenter of investor angst about everything from inflation to the debt-laden artificial-intelligence boom — and governments are paying the price.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Matthew Burgess

item.title: Copper Supply Crunch Sends Key Spread to Highest Since 2021
item.description: The copper market had another volatile session, with a key one-day spread spiking to levels last seen during a historic squeeze in 2021.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Gold Edges Below $4,400 as Traders Eye Slump in Long-Dated Bonds
item.description: Gold edged below $4,400 an ounce, as traders weighed the outlook for US inflation and interest rates while long-duration government bond yields climbed around the world.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie and Jack Ryan

item.title: Stocks Fall as Bond Selloff Saps Risk Appetite: Markets Wrap
item.description: Technology stocks drove declines in global equities as long-dated bond yields pushed further into multidecade highs and oil prices extended their climb, draining traders’ appetite for risky assets.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren and Will Standring

item.title: Technology Stocks Lift Equities, Mideast Peace Prospects Wane | The Opening Trade 8/17/2026
item.description:
Technology stocks lifted global equities after stellar revenue growth at Anthropic PBC bolstered the view that massive spending on artificial intelligence will be sustained.
Fighting between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah flared in Lebanon over the weekend, the latest setback in efforts to end parallel wars in the Middle East.
Israel’s military said Sunday that it killed Abu Hassan Alaa, a senior Hezbollah commander, in southern Lebanon a day earlier. Eleven people died in the Israeli strikes.
Corrects a graphic at 23:35: The next UK budget will be released in October.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)
